To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the interaction of oppositely charged polyions with multisensitive core-shell poly(N-isoproylacrylamide)-b-poly(methacrylic acid) microgels can be tuned with respect to charge density and distribution.

the architecture of the microgels has a significant influence of the interaction of the microgela oppositely charged polydiallyldimethyl ammonium chloride (PDADMAC), and the microgel's architecture can be used to tune the uptake and release of oppositely charged polymers.

microgels with a charged core and neutral shell can be used to absorb and encapsulate oppositely charged low molecular weight polyelectro-lytes, whereas microgels with charged shells can be used to form polyelectro lyte complexes that are similar to rigid colloidal particles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of microgels with a complex architecture.
the development and application of stimuli-sensitive microgels and microgel-based systems.
the preparation and characterization of microgels with different architecture and the investigation of their interaction with oppositively charged polyelectroltyes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the interaction of microgels with polyelectro-lytes is a complex process that is influenced by many different factors, including the microgel's architecture, its charge, its temperature sensitivity, and the polyelectrole's charge and molar mass.
the microgel's architecture determines the mechanism of polyelectroltye uptake and thus the properties of the microgel-poyelectrolyte complex.

the architecture of the microgels plays a significant role in determining the interaction with opposite-charged polyelectro-lytes and that the resulting complexes are very sensitive to the polyelectrol-lyte's molecular mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the ability to prepare multisensitive core-shell colloids with a charged core and neutral shell.
the microgels with charged shell are similar to rigid particles.

we have shown that microgels can be prepared that combine temperature sensitivity with pH sensitivity, and we have shown that these microgels can interact with oppositely charge polyelectro-lytes in different ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that

microgels with a neutral core and charged shell are ideal for polyelectro lyte encapsulation, whereas microgels with the charged core and neutral shell are ideal for encapsulation of charged molecules.
the architecture of the microgels has a significant influence not only on their properties but also on the interaction with other charged species.
the microgel architecture has a strong impact on the interaction with polyelectrolys, and thus, it can be used to tune the properties of microgel-polyeletrolyte complexes.
